sources.entry: We overestimate our short-term ability, but underestimate our long-term ability.

summary.title: OSTA/ULTA
summary.one_liner: People overestimate short-term output and underestimate long-term gains, so steady, paced habits and quantity-first practice beat scattered bursts of effort.
keywords: how to build habits that last
takeaways: People tend to overestimate what they can do in a short burst and underestimate what steady effort compounds into over months.
Pace habits like exercise and creative work; cramming a lot into one weekend is hard to sustain and risks burnout.
Early in a creative practice, prioritise quantity: making many pieces teaches you more than trying to make one perfect piece.
Set calling a piece 'done' as a rule so you can move on to the next one; done is better than perfect.
Relying on external deadlines or crowdfunding for motivation can lead to last-minute rushing; build a sustainable routine instead.
summary.summary: This personal blog post by a designer reflects on why their scattered side projects led to rushed, stressful work. They describe a shift toward two 2023 goals, gym twice a week and 52 YouTube videos, and explain the idea "we overestimate our short-term ability, but underestimate our long-term ability." The post supports this with their own experience of improving through weekly practice and cites Ali Abdaal's compounding-1% idea and a potter anecdote about quantity leading to quality. It ends with three personal mottos: SIFI, OSTA/ULTA and DIBTP.
